I will keep the land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County that is the most familiar and reliable way for me to farm, and at 76 I would rather choose a steady system I already understand than chase something labor-heavy or risky. I will use improved seed, not the cheapest traditional seed and not high-risk specialty crops. For wheat, I will focus on base fertilizer, one topdressing at jointing, two or three irrigations depending on rain, and a few pesticide sprays only when disease or insects show up. After wheat harvest, I will quickly plant summer maize on the same land, keep fertilizer balanced, irrigate a couple of times if the summer rain is not enough, and manage weeds and insects with a small number of sprays. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and lighter for me than deep ploughing, and it fits a simple wheat-maize cycle.
